NASHR:v2p310/r19.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p310/r19.speaker: أبو جعفر وعاصم وروح
NASHR:v2p310/r19.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, ʿĀṣim, and Rawḥ open both consonants in thamar; Ruways agrees in the first occurrence only.
NASHR:v2p310/r19.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر وعاصم وروح بفتح الثاء والميم، وافقهم رويس في الأول

NASHR:v2p310/r20.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p310/r20.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p310/r20.claim: Abu ʿAmr uses damma on the tha and sukun on the mim in both occurrences.
NASHR:v2p310/r20.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بضم الثاء، وإسكان الميم فيهما

NASHR:v2p310/r21.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p310/r21.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p310/r21.claim: The remaining readers put damma on both the tha and mim in both occurrences.
NASHR:v2p310/r21.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بضم الثاء والميم في الموضعين

IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads ثمر and بثمره with ḍamma on thāʾ and sukūn on mīm; some transmissions from him match Nāfiʿ instead.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r5.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ﴿ ثمر ﴾ و ﴿ بثمره ﴾ بضم الثاء وسكون الميم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r6.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r6.claim: These readers use ḍamma on both thāʾ and mīm in ثمر and بثمره.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائى ﴿ ثمر ﴾ و ﴿ بثمره ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r7.speaker: عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r7.claim: ʿĀṣim reads ثمر and بثمره with fatḥa on both thāʾ and mīm.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r7.anchor: وقرأ عاصم ﴿ ثمر ﴾ و ﴿ بثمره ﴾ بفتح الثاء والميم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r6.claim: Muḥāwarah means exchanging speech, from the root meaning to return.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r6.anchor: المحاورة: مراجعة الكلام من حار إذا رجع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r9.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وابن كثير ونافع وجماعة قراء المدينة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r9.claim: These readers pronounce thumar with ḍamma on both consonants, a plural of thimār.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وابن كثير ونافع وجماعة قراء المدينة: ثمر وبثمره بضم الثاء والميم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r10.speaker: الأعمش وأبو رجاء وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r10.claim: These readers use a still mīm, either as a lightened form or as the plural of thamarah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r10.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وأبو رجاء وأبو عمرو بإسكان الميم فيهما تخفيفا أو جمع ثمرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر والحسن وجابر بن زيد والحجاج وعاصم وأبو حاتم ويعقوب عن رويس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r11.claim: This group reads both forms with fatḥa on thāʾ and mīm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر والحسن وجابر بن زيد والحجاج وعاصم وأبو حاتم ويعقوب عن رويس عنه بفتح الثاء والميم فيهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r12.speaker: رويس عن يعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r12.claim: Ruwais transmits ḍamma on both letters in thumar but fatḥa in bithamarihi for readers using the ḍamma form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r12.anchor: قرأ رويس عن يعقوب ثمر بضمهما وبثمره بفتحهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r13.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda gloss thamar as all wealth, including gold and livestock.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة الثمر جميع المال من الذهب والحيوان وغير ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r1.claim: Mujāhid restricts thamar to gold and silver.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r1.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يراد بها الذهب والفضة خاصة. وقال ابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd takes it as the trees' underlying stock or roots bearing fruit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r2.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: هي الأصول فيها الثمر. وقال أبو عمرو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ glosses thamar as wealth; on that reading the man had abundant assets to maintain the gardens.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: الثمر المال، فعلى هذا المعنى أنه كانت له إلى الجنتين أموال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r4.claim: The fatḥa reading unambiguously means the fruit borne by the trees.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r4.anchor: وأما من قرأ بالفتح فلا إشكال أنه يعني به حمل الشجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r5.speaker: أبو رجاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r5.claim: Abū Rajāʾ has a transmitted reading with fatḥa on thāʾ and a still mīm; Ubayy's codex has a gloss meaning abundant fruit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء في رواية ثمر بفتح الثاء وسكون الميم، وفي مصحف أبي وآتيناه ثمرا كثيرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r6.claim: The phrase about speaking to his companion indicates that the two were not brothers; the stated disputation is apparently the rich man's denial of resurrection and associationism.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r6.anchor: ويظهر من قوله فقال لصاحبه أنه ليس أخاه، وهو يحاوره جملة حالية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r7.claim: An alternative makes the circumstantial clause describe the Muslim companion, who disputes with him by preaching belief in God and resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r7.anchor: وقيل: هي حال من صاحبه أي المسلم كان يحاوره بالوعظ والدعاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r8.claim: The companion apparently also had wealth and followers, contrary to historical reports that he was a destitute petitioner; the comparison in the text supports this reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r8.anchor: والظاهر كون أفعل للتفضيل وأن صاحبه كان له مال ونفر ولم يكن سبروتا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r9.claim: The rich man's boast reflects unbelievers' pride in wealth and clan, as in Quraysh leaders' demand that the Prophet remove Salman and his poor companions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r9.anchor: وهذا على عادة الكفار في الافتخار بكثرة المال وعزة العشيرة والتكبر والاغترار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r10.claim: Nafr can mean supporters and attendants, or male children who accompany their father; interpreting it as a shared clan would undermine the argument that the two were not brothers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r10.anchor: وعنى بالنفر أنصاره وحشمه. وقيل: أولادا ذكورا لأنهم ينفرون معه دون الإناث

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171#2/r1.claim: The garden owner tells his believing companion he has more wealth and a stronger following; nafar can mean kin or clan.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171#2/r1.anchor: {فقال} يعني صاحب البستان {لصاحبه} المؤمن {وهو يحاوره} يخاطبه ويجاوبه: {أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا} أي: عشيرة ورهطا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171#2/r2.claim: He interprets nafar as servants and attendants.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171#2/r3.claim: He interprets nafar as children, supported by the later mention of wealth and offspring.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171#2/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: ولدا تصديقه قوله تعالى: "إن ترن أنا أقل منك مالا وولدا"

JISHUMI:v6p4411/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r2.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r2.claim: One interpretation of ثمر is the dates among the garden's produce.
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r2.anchor: ثمر من النخل الذي فيهما، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v6p4411/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r3.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r3.claim: Mujahid interprets ثمر as gold and silver.

JISHUMI:v6p4411/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، وقتادة
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada interpret ثمر as varied kinds of wealth.
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r4.anchor: صنوف الأموال، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v6p4411/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r5.claim: The gardens also contained kinds of trees besides grapes and palms.
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r5.anchor: في الجنتين سوى الأعناب والنخيل من سائر صنوف الأشجار

JISHUMI:v6p4411/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r6.claim: Nafar is interpreted as one's clan and relatives.

JISHUMI:v6p4411/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r7.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r7.claim: Qatada interprets nafar as servants and attendants.

JISHUMI:v6p4411/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r8.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v6p4411/r8.claim: Muqatil interprets nafar as children, matching the later mention of wealth and offspring.

TABATABAI:18:42-44/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r6.claim: The companion’s words verbally correct the man’s claims, while the garden’s ruin demonstrates the error in expecting worldly permanence, trusting wealth and followers, and claiming self-sufficiency.
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r6.anchor: بيانا قوليا لخطأ الرجل في كفره وشركه

THALABI:v6p170#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p170#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p170#2/r1.claim: The wealthy garden owner, identified as Fatrus, shows his Muslim companion the garden and assumes it will never perish; he doubts the Hour and expects a better return if raised.
THALABI:v6p170#2/r1.anchor: ودخل جنته، يعني: فطروس، أخذ بيد أخيه المسلم يطوف به ويريه إياها

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The two-person parable exposes opponents who take worldly success as proof of their beliefs, infer that the afterlife is imaginary, or expect to fare better there than believers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: they regarded their worldly success to be proof of the veracity of their ideology and deeds; when Muslims would warn them of God and the Hereafter, they would reply that since they were better off than them in worldly affairs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The parable mirrors Quraysh’s outward and inward arrogance and the conflict between truth and falsehood; the poor companion has faith and joy in knowing God despite lacking orchards.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The arrogant among the Quraysh are narrated a parable here which mirrors their inner and outer selves and also makes them see the fate of the conflict between truth and falsehood

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The orchard owner should have responded to God’s favour with gratitude, but instead argued when his companion urged gratitude and warned of divine wrath for ingratitude.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: what should have been expected from him was an expression of immense gratitude to the God Who blessed him with this favour. However, what actually happened

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The word for its fruit indicates that the exchange occurred when the crop was ready for harvest, when affluence especially intoxicates an orchard owner.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: when the crops were ready for harvesting. Obviously, on such occasions, the owner of an orchard becomes all the more inebriated with his affluence.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The orchard owner arrogantly thought his lush garden indestructible, while Dhū al-Qarnayn is the grateful servant who credits his achievement to God and remembers God’s certain promise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the mentality of one of them was inflicted with arrogance: when he entered enter his lush orchard, he would haughtily say that he does not think that it will ever be destroyed.

BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r3.claim: ثمر includes kinds of wealth beyond the gardens; explicitly mentioning produce signals his abundant harvest and other assets.
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r3.anchor: وذكرها وإن كانت الجنة لا تخلو عنها إيذان بكثرة الحاصل له

BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r4.claim: Al-Kashifi says he had every kind of fruit, including grapes, dates, and others, named because these were most prominent.

BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r5.claim: The companion is the believing brother; يحاوره means conversing and answering back, which explains the description of their exchange.
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r5.anchor: يكلمه ويراجعه الكلام من حار إذا رجع

BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r6.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan defines wealth broadly as all owned goods and property, while al-mal al-ayn is specifically coined money.
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن الحسن رحمه الله : المال كله ما يتملكه الناس

BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r7.claim: Nafar means male helpers, sons, or retinue, conventionally three to ten men and not more.
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r7.anchor: والنفر بفتحتين من الثلاثة إلى العشرة من الرجال

BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r8.claim: The author sees a difficulty if the comparative is literal: two actual brothers inherited equal shares, so the believer should not have had no wealth while the unbeliever had more; he leaves the answer unresolved.
BURSEVI:v5p189#3/r8.anchor: لاح لي ههنا إشكال وهو أنه إن حمل أفعل على حقيقته

ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r1.claim: Thamar means kinds of wealth, not tree produce, which does not fit the passage.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r1.anchor: ثمر ( أنواع المال كما في القاموس وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r2.claim: The reading thumur denotes abundant wealth such as gold, silver, and livestock; Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda explain it so.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r2.anchor: وبذلك فسره ابن عباس وقتادة وغيرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid restricts thumur to gold and silver.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد يراد به الذهب والفضة خاصة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r4.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r4.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Abū Rajāʾ, and Abū ʿAmr read thumur with still mīm; Abū Rajāʾ also has a fatḥa-and-sukūn variant, with the same meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وأبو رجاء وأبو عمرو بضم الثاء وإسكان الميم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r5.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r5.claim: Ubayy’s codex has the explanatory phrase wa-ātaynāhu thamanan kathīran, We gave him abundant wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r5.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي وحمل على التفسير ( وآتيناه ثمرا كثيرا )

ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r6.claim: His companion is the believer; the lexical sense of companion does not rule out the men being brothers. Yuḥāwiruhu denotes reciprocal speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r6.anchor: والمراد بالصاحب المعنى اللغوي فلا ينافي هذا العنوان القول بأنهما كانا أخوين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r7.claim: Nafar means attendants and helpers, or male children according to Qatāda and Muqātil, or the man’s clan.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r7.anchor: حشما وأعوانا وقيل : أولادا ذكورا وروي ذلك عن قتادة ومقاتل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r8.claim: Mālan and nafaran are accusative specifications; the comparative apparently has its literal sense, conflicting with reports that the believer remained destitute after giving away his wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p274#2/r8.anchor: ونصب ( مالا ونفرا ) على التمييز وهو على ما قيل محول

ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r5.speaker: النيسابوري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r5.claim: Al-Nīsābūrī reads the gardens as desire and world, fruit as cravings, boasting of wealth and status as inclination and blameworthy traits, expecting a better garden as delusion about God, and turning hands over as regret for wasted life and good potential.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r5.anchor: قال ذلك غرورا بالله تعالى وكرمه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r4.speaker: عاصم وأبو جعفر ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r4.claim: These readers open both consonants in thamar, making it a plural of fruit that the trees produce for eating.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r4.anchor: وكان له} لصاحب البستان {ثمر} قرأ عاصم وأبو جعفر ويعقوب {ثمر} بفتح الثاء والميم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r5.claim: Abu Amr reads thamar with a damma on the first letter and a silent second, meaning abundant productive wealth of many kinds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: بضم الثاء ساكنة الميم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r6.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r6.claim: The other readers use a damma on both letters, taking it as many kinds of fruitful wealth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r6.anchor: ومن قرأ بالضم فهي الأموال الكثيرة المثمرة من كل صنف جمع ثمار.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r7.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r7.claim: Mujahid says the owner's wealth was gold and silver; another gloss says all kinds of fruit.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ذهب وفضة وقيل: جميع الثمرات.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r8.speaker: الأزهري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r8.claim: Al-Azhari explains the plural formation: thamara becomes thamar, then thimar, then again thamar.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p171/r8.anchor: قال الأزهري: "الثمرة" تجمع على "ثمر" ويجمع "الثمر" على "ثمار" ثم تجمع "الثمار" على "ثمر"

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:33-34/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:33-34/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:33-34/r5.claim: Thamar means other kinds of property besides the gardens; ʿĀṣim opens both consonants, Abu ʿAmr dammas the first and quiesces the second, and others damma both, also at 18:42.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:33-34/r5.anchor: وقرأ عاصم بفتح الثاء والميم، وأبو عمرو بضم الثاء وإسكان الميم

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:33-34/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:33-34/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:33-34/r6.claim: Muḥāwaratan means returning speech in dialogue, from the root meaning to return.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:33-34/r6.anchor: يراجعه في الكلام من حار إذا رجع

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:33-34/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:33-34/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:33-34/r7.claim: Nafar means retinue and supporters, or male children because they accompany him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:33-34/r7.anchor: حشما وأعوانا. وقيل أولادا ذكورا لأنهم الذين ينفرون معه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r3.claim: The owner has additional abundant, varied productive wealth beyond the gardens, enabling him to hire workers and obtain tools.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r3.anchor: وكان له } أي صاحب الجنتين { ثمر } أي مال مثمر غير ما تقدم كثير , ذو أنواع

BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r4.claim: The unbelieving owner boasts to the Muslim companion, represented as a poor believer, that he has more wealth and a stronger retinue.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r4.anchor: فقال } أي هذا الكافر { لصاحبه } أي المسلم المجعول مثلا لفقراء المؤمنين

DURR-FULL:v5p390/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p390/r4.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
DURR-FULL:v5p390/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {وكان له ثمر} يقول: مال

DURR-FULL:v5p390/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p390/r5.speaker: قتادة رضي الله عنه
DURR-FULL:v5p390/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas read thamar with ḍamma, meaning kinds of wealth.
DURR-FULL:v5p390/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه قال: قرأها ابن عباس {وكان له ثمر} بالضم يعني أنواع المال

DURR-FULL:v5p390/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p390/r6.speaker: مجاهد رضي الله عنه
DURR-FULL:v5p390/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {وكان له ثمر} قال: ذهب وفضة

DURR-FULL:v5p390/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p390/r7.speaker: بشير بن عبيد
DURR-FULL:v5p390/r7.claim: Bashir read thamar in the nominative: thamar means wealth, children, and slaves, whereas thumur means fruit.
DURR-FULL:v5p390/r7.anchor: عن بشير بن عبيد أنه كان قرأ {وكان له ثمر} برفع الثاء وقال: الثمر المال والولدان والرقيق

DURR-FULL:v5p390/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p390/r8.speaker: أبو يزيد المدني
DURR-FULL:v5p390/r8.claim: Abu Yazid distinguishes the tree's stock from its fruit in his reading and gloss.
DURR-FULL:v5p390/r8.anchor: عن أبي يزيد المدني أنه كان يقرؤها {وكان له ثمر} قال: الأصل والثمر الثمرة

QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r2.claim: Outwardly, one of two garden owners thanked his Creator while the other disbelieved his Provider; the latter's garden was ruined and he regretted neglecting gratitude.
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r2.anchor: فشكر أحدهما لخالقه وكفر الآخر برازقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r1.claim: Thamar with two dammas means abundant, varied wealth, including money, livestock, gardens, and fields; it figuratively derives from the fruiting of one's assets.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r1.anchor: والثمر بضم الثاء والميم : المال الكثير المختلف من النقدين والأنعام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r2.claim: Nabigha's verse attests the metaphor of wealth bearing fruit, and his other line uses athmara for wealth and children.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r2.anchor: قال النابغة : فلما رأى أن ثمر الله ماله وأثل موجودا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r3.claim: The majority read thamar with two dammas; Abu Amr and Yaqub use a sukun on the second consonant, while Asim reads both vowels as fatha, with the latter taken as a plural indicating many kinds of earnings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { ثمر } بضم المثلثة وضم الميم . وقرأه أبو عمرو ويعقوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r4.speaker: ثعلب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r4.claim: Thaalab recounts that al-Hajjaj threatened to cut the tongue of anyone reading thamar with two dammas; al-A'mash's response was not to follow that threat and he used that reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r4.anchor: وعن النحاس بسنده إلى ثعلب عن الأعمش : أن الحجاح قال : لو سمعت أحدا يقرأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r5.claim: The owner had additional wealth besides the two gardens; the preceding abundance naturally led him to boast, and sahib here means the other man paired with him in the parable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p318/r5.anchor: والمعنى : وكان لصاحب الجنتين مال ، أي غير الجنتين . والفاء لتفريع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p319/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p319/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p319/r1.claim: The dialogue shows the poorer man had admonished his companion about faith and righteous conduct; the rich man answered with arrogance rather than fair argument.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p319/r1.anchor: ودل فعل المحاورة على أن صاحبه قد وعظه في الإيمان والعمل الصالح ، فراجعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p319/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p319/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p319/r2.claim: A'azz means greater in strength and honor, linked to numerous kin and courage; nafar means the man's fighting kin and here his sons, as verse 40 confirms, and it is a specification of the comparison.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p319/r2.anchor: والنفر : عشيرة الرجل الذين ينفرون معه . وأراد بهم هنا ولده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r3.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r3.claim: They read thamar with ḍamma on both letters as plural of thimār; others use mīm sukūn as lightening, perhaps plural of thamarah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وابن عباس ومجاهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r4.speaker: عاصم وأبو جعفر والحسن وجابر بن زيد والحجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r4.claim: They read thamar with fatḥa on both letters, meaning tree fruit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r4.anchor: وقرأ عاصم «ثمر» وبثمره يفتح الميم والثاء فيهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r5.claim: They take thumur as all wealth including gold, silver, and livestock; they cite al-Nābigha.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r5.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وقتادة: «الثمر» جميع المال من الذهب والفضة والحيوان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r6.claim: Mujāhid restricts thumur to gold and silver.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد يراد بها الذهب والفضة خاصة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says thumur means the rootstock that bears fruit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد «الثمر» هي الأصول التي فيها الثمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r8.claim: With fatḥa, thamar means fruit; mentioning fruit economically implies destruction of roots supplying future yields.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r8.anchor: فلا إشكال في أن المعنى ما في رؤوس الشجر من الأكل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r9.speaker: أبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r9.claim: Ubayy's codex says God gave him abundant fruit or wealth.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r10.speaker: أبو رجاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r10.claim: Abū Rajāʾ reads thamar with fatḥa on thāʾ and sukūn on mīm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء «وكان له ثمر» بفتح الثاء وسكون الميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r11.claim: Muḥāwara means exchange of speech and derives from ḥāra-yaḥūru.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r11.anchor: والمحاورة مراجعة القول، وهو من حار يحور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r12.claim: Some infer “more men” means the pair were not brothers; the reply says nafar means servants who fulfill his needs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r12.anchor: واستدل بعض الناس من قوله وأعز نفرا على أنه لم يكن أخاه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516/r13.claim: The boast displays arrogance and parallels ʿUyayna and al-Aqraʿ telling the Prophet to dismiss Salmān and companions.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r1.claim: These readers pronounce thamar with ḍamma in both occurrences; Asim uses fatḥa, and Abu Amr reads one form with a single ḍamma and a still mīm.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وكان له ثمر وأحيط بثمره بضمتين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r2.claim: Al-Farra says fatḥa means edible fruit and ḍamma means wealth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r2.anchor: قال الفراء الثمر بفتح التاء والميم المأكول وبضمها المال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says fatḥa can be a collective and ḍamma a plural, while thumar can mean fruit or collected wealth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r3.anchor: الثمر بالفتح الجمع الاول والثمر بالضم جمع الثمر يقال ثمر وثمر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r4.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi allows thumar to be a plural of fruits or of a single fruit, or a singular noun itself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r4.anchor: قراءة أبي عمرو ثمر يجوز أن تكون جمع ثمار ككتاب وكتب فتخفف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r5.claim: On the ḍamma reading, Ibn Abbas says thamar means abundant wealth of various kinds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r5.anchor: أنه المال الكثير من صنوف الأموال قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r6.claim: Mujahid identifies thamar as gold and silver.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says thamar can be the plural of fruit, with the forms thamarah, thimār, and thamar.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r7.anchor: أنه جمع ثمرة قال الزجاج يقال ثمرة وثمار وثمر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r8.claim: One explanation for mentioning thamar after the gardens is that he did not own the land itself, only its yield; Ibn Abbas reports this.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r8.anchor: أنه لم يكن أصل الأرض ملكا له وإنما كانت له الثمار قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the mention emphasizes the abundance of his fruit in the two gardens and elsewhere.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r9.anchor: أن ذكر الثمر دليل على كثرة ما يملك من الثمار في الجنتين وغيرهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r10.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r10.claim: A third explanation takes thamar as gold and silver, metaphorically named for their increase; however fruit fits better because the verse mentions what he spent there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r10.anchor: من قال هو الذهب والورق فانما قيل لذلك ثمر على التفاؤول لأن الثمر نماء في ذي الثمر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r11.claim: The boastful man is the unbelieving brother, who converses by answering back and exchanging words with the believer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p140/r11.anchor: فقال يعني الكافر لصاحبه المؤمن وهو يحاوره أي يراجعه الكلام ويجاوبه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r1.claim: The two men’s conversation concerned either faith and unbelief or pursuit of worldly life versus the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنه الايمان والكفر والثاني طلب الدنيا وطلب الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r2.claim: Ibn Faris says nafar means several men, between three and ten; qawm and raht are similar terms without a singular of the same form.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r2.anchor: النفر عدة رجال من ثلاثة إلى العشرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the man’s followers were his servants.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r4.claim: Muqatil says the man’s followers were his children.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r5.speaker: أبو سليمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p142/r5.claim: Abu Sulayman says the followers were his clan and kin.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada say the man’s thamar means wealth; Ibn Kathir says fruits is clearer in context, supported by a variant reading with thāʾ vocalized and mīm still.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r3.anchor: قيل: المراد به: المال. روي عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة. وقيل: الثمار وهو أظهر هاهنا، ويؤيده القراءة الأخرى:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r4.speaker: قراء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r4.claim: Readers differ on thamar: one variant has thāʾ with ḍamma and mīm still, making it a plural of fruit, while others read both consonants with fatḥa.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r4.anchor: "وكان له ثمر" بضم الثاء وتسكين الميم، فيكون (5) جمع ثمرة، كخشبة وخشب، وقرأ آخرون: {ثمر} بفتح الثاء والميم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r5.claim: The garden owner disputes and boasts that he has more wealth and a stronger retinue, meaning more servants, attendants, and children.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r5.anchor: أي: يجادله ويخاصمه، يفتخر عليه ويترأس: {أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا} أي: أكثر خدما وحشما وولدا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r6.claim: Qatada calls abundant wealth and a powerful retinue the wicked man’s aspiration.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r6.anchor: قال قتادة: تلك -والله-أمنية الفاجر: كثرة المال وعزة النفر.

JISHUMI:v6p4407/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r7.claim: Abu Ja‘far, Asim, and Ya‘qub read ثمر with fatḥa in both occurrences as a plural of ثمار.
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وعاصم ويعقوب: وكان له ثمر، وأحيط بثمره بفتح الثاء والميم في الحرفين جميعا، وهو جمع ثمار،

JISHUMI:v6p4407/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r8.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r8.claim: One report from Ya‘qub distinguishes the two forms, reading the first with fatḥa and the second with ḍamma.
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r8.anchor: وروي عن يعقوب: (كان له ثمر)، بفتح الثاء والميم وأحيط بثمره بضم الثاء والميم،

JISHUMI:v6p4407/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r9.claim: Abu Amr reads both forms with ḍamma; the same reading is reported for the remaining readers.
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بضم الثاء والميم في الحرفين، وقرأ الباقون بضم الثاء والميم في الحرفين

JISHUMI:v6p4407/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r10.claim: The ḍamma form may be a plural of ثمار or of ثمر, like حمر and خشب.
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r10.anchor: وهو جمع: ثمار وثمر نحو: حمار وحمر، ونحو أن يكون جمع ثمر كخشب وخشب.

JISHUMI:v6p4409/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r3.claim: Muḥāwara is reciprocal conversation; one may describe speech that receives no response as having no dialogue.
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r3.anchor: والمحاورة: مراجعة الكلام في المخاطبة، يقال: كلمت فلانا فما رجع إلي حوارا

JISHUMI:v6p4409/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r11.claim: The brothers inherited wealth; one spent it for God while the other mocked him. The story is connected with 37:50.
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r11.anchor: فكانت قصتهما أنهما كانا أخوين ورثا مالا، فأنفق المؤمن من ماله في سبيل الله

AKHFASH:v2p430#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p430#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p430#2/r1.claim: The parable mentions two men, but only one had fruit; mentioning both in the setup suffices for the singular وكان له ثمر.
AKHFASH:v2p430#2/r1.anchor: وقوله {واضرب لهم مثلا رجلين} وقال {وكان له ثمر} وإنما ذكر الرجلين في المعنى وكان لأحدهما ثمر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r11.claim: Thamar means multiple kinds of wealth; Mujahid says the man had gold and silver in addition to the two gardens, making him wealthy enough to develop land as he pleased.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r11.anchor: وعن مجاهد : الذهب والفضة ، أي : كانت له إلى الجنتين الموصوفتين الأموال الدثرة من الذهب والفضة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r12.claim: Nufr may mean supporters and retinue, or sons because they accompany their father unlike daughters; yuhāwiruhu means exchanging speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r12.anchor: وأعز نفرا } يعني أنصارا وحشما . وقيل : أولادا ذكورا ، لأنهم ينفرون معه دون الإناث ، يحاوره : يراجعه الكلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r10.speaker: عاصم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r10.claim: Asim reads ثمر with both thāʾ and mīm open.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r11.speaker: أبو عمرو
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r11.claim: Abu Amr reads ثمر with thāʾ damma and mīm sukun.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بضم الثاء وإسكان الميم ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r12.speaker: الباقون
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r12.claim: The remaining readers pronounce both thāʾ and mīm with damma.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ الباقون ثمر بضم الثاء والميم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r13.claim: One view treats the open and rounded readings as equivalent in meaning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r13.anchor: أحدهما : معناهما واحد , فعلى هذا فيه ثلاثة تأويلات

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r14.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r14.claim: On the equivalent-meaning view, ثمر can mean gold and silver, wealth that yields returns.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r14.anchor: أحدها : أنه الذهب والفضة , قاله قتادة , لأنها أموال مثمرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r15.claim: Another equivalent-meaning gloss is abundant wealth of varied kinds, whose increase is greater.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r15.anchor: الثاني : أنه المال الكثير من صنوف الأموال , قاله ابن عباس لأن تثميره أكثر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r16.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r16.claim: Another equivalent-meaning gloss is principal wealth that produces growth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r16.anchor: الثالث : أنه الأصل الذي له نماء , قاله ابن زيد , لأن في النماء تثميرا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r17.claim: A competing view says the readings differ: the open form is a plural of ثَمرة, while the rounded form is a plural of ثمار.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r17.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن معناهما بالضم وبالفتح مختلف , فعلى هذا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r18.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r18.claim: On the differing-meaning view, the open form means date-palm fruit, while the rounded form means all wealth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r18.anchor: الثاني : أنه بالفتح ثمار النخيل خاصة , وبالضم جميع الأموال , قاله ابن بحر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r19.claim: Another distinction is that the open form means fruit borne by its own tree, the rounded form fruit acquired from elsewhere.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r19.anchor: الثالث : أنه بالفتح ما كان ثماره من أصله , وبالضم ما كان ثماره من غيره .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r20.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r20.claim: A further distinction takes rounded ثمر as the root or stock, and open ثمر as the branch or yield.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r20.anchor: الرابع : أن الثمر بالضم الأصل , وبالفتح الفرع , قاله ابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r21.speaker: الجمهور
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r21.claim: Most commentators take his ثمر to mean produce from the two gardens already mentioned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r21.anchor: أحدهما : أنه ثمر الجنتين المتقدم ذكرهما , وهو قول الجمهور .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r22.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r22.claim: Alternatively, it includes produce he owned without owning its trees, broadening the total wealth to include others' property.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r22.anchor: الثاني : أنه ثمر ملكه من غير جنتيه , وأصله كان لغيره كما يملك الناس ثمارا لا يملكون أصولها , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r23.claim: The companion is the man's Muslim brother, who spent wealth seeking afterlife reward; the garden owner was an unbeliever who spent to preserve worldly status and compete in abundance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r23.anchor: يعني لأخيه المسلم الذي صرف ماله في القرب طلبا للثواب في الآخرة ، وصرف هذا الكافر ماله فيما استبقاه للدنيا والمكاثرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r24.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r24.claim: يُحاور means that the man was debating his companion.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r25.claim: The debate may have concerned belief and unbelief, or worldly pursuit and pursuit of the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r25.anchor: وفيما يحاوره فيه وجهان : أحدهما : في الإيمان والكفر . الثاني : في طلب الدنيا وطلب الآخرة ,

FARRA:v2p144/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p144/r2.speaker: مجاهد
FARRA:v2p144/r2.claim: Mujahid says thamar with ḍamma means wealth, while thamar with fatḥa means fruit.
FARRA:v2p144/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: ما كان في القرآن من ثمر بالضم فهو مال، وما كان من ثمر مفتوح فهو من الثمار.

MUJAHID:v1p376#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p376#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p376#3/r1.claim: Mujahid explains the garden owner's thamar as gold and silver.
MUJAHID:v1p376#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وكان له ثمر ﴾ يعني ذهبا وفضة

MUQATIL:18:34-37/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r1.claim: The unbeliever's thamar was wealth in gold, silver, and other kinds of property.
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r1.anchor: وكان للكافر مال من الذهب والفضة، وغيرها من أصناف الأموال

MUQATIL:18:34-37/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r2.claim: After becoming poor, the believer came to his brother seeking generosity; the account contrasts his worn state with the unbeliever's fine clothes and mount.
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r2.anchor: فلما افتقر المؤمن، أتى أخاه الكافر متعرضا لمعروفه

MUQATIL:18:34-37/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r3.claim: The believer says he lent his inheritance to God, the faithful and enduring, for himself and his children; the unbeliever mocks this belief as waste.
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r3.anchor: أقرضته إلهي الملي الوفي، فقدمته لنفسي ولولدي

MUQATIL:18:34-37/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r4.claim: The companion is the believing brother, and يحاوره means answering or conversing back and forth.

MUQATIL:18:34-37/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r5.claim: The unbeliever's boast of greater wealth and standing includes having more children.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r1.claim: ثمر refers to abundant kinds of wealth, including gold, silver, and other possessions beyond the gardens.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r1.anchor: لصاحب الجنتين ثمر أنواع من المال من ثمر ماله إذا كثره أي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r2.speaker: عاصم
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r2.claim: ʿAsim reads ثمر with fatḥ on both the tāʾ and mīm; Abu ʿAmr has ḍamma on tāʾ and sukūn on mīm, and the others have ḍamma on both.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r2.anchor: وأحيط بثمره بفتح الميم والثاء عاصم وبضم الثاء وسكون الميم أبو عمرو وبضمهما غيرهما

NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r3.claim: The two men’s dialogue is reciprocal speech; Qutrus takes the believer around the gardens to show them off and boast of his greater wealth.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r3.anchor: يراجعه الكلام من حار يحور إذا رجع يعني قطروس أخذ بيد المسلم يطوف به في الجنتين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r4.claim: More followers and retinue are one meaning of نفرا; alternatively it means male children, who accompany him unlike daughters.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13#3/r4.anchor: أنصارا وحشما أو أولادا ذكورا لأنهم ينفرون معه دون الاناث

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r1.claim: The parable concerns those proud of worldly goods who disdain sitting with believers; it connects with the command to remain patient with believers.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r1.anchor: هذا مثل لمن يتعزز بالدنيا ويستنكف عن مجالسة المؤمنين، وهو متصل بقوله { واصبر نفسك }.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r2.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says it was revealed about Makhzumi brothers in Mecca: believer Abu Salama and unbeliever al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad; each inherited four thousand dinars, one spending his share for God.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r2.anchor: فقال الكلبي: نزلت في أخوين من أهل مكة مخزوميين، أحدهما مؤمن وهو أبو سلمة عبد الله بن عبد الأسد

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r3.claim: The brothers are linked to the companion in 37:51. Other identifications make the pair the Prophet and Meccans, all believers and disbelievers, or Uyayna's party against Salman and Suhayb.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r3.anchor: وهما الأخوان المذكوران في سورة «الصافات» في قوله قال قآئل منهم إني كان لي قرين

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r4.claim: Another account makes them Israelite brothers, with the believing brother named Judah according to Ibn Abbas and Tamlīkha according to Muqatil, and the unbeliever Qartush.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r4.anchor: شبههم الله برجلين من بني إسرائيل أخوين أحدهما مؤمن واسمه يهوذا في قول ابن عباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r5.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r5.claim: Muqatil names the brothers Tamlīkha and Qartush; one account says the believer freed slaves, clothed the naked, fed the hungry, and built mosques, while the other invested in worldly prosperity.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل: اسمه تمليخا. والآخر كافر واسمه قرطوش.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r6.claim: The impoverished believer seeks work in the rich brother's garden; the rich man mocks his faith, denies resurrection, and expels him.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r6.anchor: وأدركت الأول الحاجة، فأراد أن يستخدم نفسه في جنة يخدمها فقال: لو ذهبت لشريكي وصاحبي

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r7.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r7.claim: Ata says the two men were partners who owned eight thousand dinars.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r7.anchor: قال عطاء: كانا شريكين لهما ثمانية آلاف دينار.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r1.claim: A further story has the poor brother spend his share on heavenly land, a house, a wife, and servants and goods; the rich brother rejects belief and worships an idol.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r1.anchor: وقيل: ورثاه من أبيهما وكانا أخوين فاقتسماها، فاشترى أحدهما أرضا بألف دينار،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r2.claim: The brothers test their claims by fishing; the unbeliever catches many fish while invoking an idol, and the believer catches none while invoking God.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r2.anchor: فقال: سر بنا نصطد السمك، فمن صاد أكثر فهو على حق فقال له: يا أخي!

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r3.claim: The assigned angel protests; Gabriel shows each brother his Paradise or Hell home, and both judge worldly fortune irrelevant to that final destination.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r3.anchor: قال: فضج الملك الموكل بهما، فأمر الله تعالى جبريل أن يأخذه فيذهب به إلى الجنان

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r4.claim: God takes the believer and destroys the unbeliever; in Paradise the believer recalls his companion and asks to see him in Hell, echoing 37:51–52.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r4.anchor: ثم إن الله تعالى توفى المؤمن وأهلك الكافر بعذاب من عنده، فلما استقر المؤمن في الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r1.claim: The present surah describes the brothers' worldly condition, while 37:51–61 describes their afterlife condition.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r1.anchor: بين الله تعالى حال الأخوين في الدنيا في هذه السورة، وبين حالهما في الآخرة في سورة «الصافات»

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya cites a report that Lake Tinnis was the gardens; one brother sold his share, spent in obedience, was mocked, and the lake flooded overnight.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وذكر إبراهيم بن القاسم الكاتب في كتابه في عجائب البلاد أن بحيرة تنيس كانت هاتين الجنتين،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r3.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r3.claim: Al-Mawardi says the story may be a parable for this community urging renunciation of worldly life and desire for the hereafter; Qurtubi says the context argues otherwise.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r3.anchor: وقد قيل: إن هذا مثل ضربه الله تعالى لهذه الأمة، وليس بخبر عن حال متقدمة،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r4.claim: Palms surrounded the gardens, with crops among grapevines; حفاف means a side or encircling edge.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r4.anchor: { وحففناهما بنخل } أي أطفناهما من جوانبهما بنخل. والحفاف الجانب،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r5.claim: كلتا means each garden; singular آتت supports the Basran view that كلا and كلتا are singular forms denoting a pair.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r5.anchor: { كلتا الجنتين } أي كل واحدة من الجنتين { آتت أكلها } تاما، ولذلك لم يقل آتتا.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r6.speaker: أهل البصرة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r6.claim: Basrans treat كلا and كلتا as singular forms emphasizing two, inflected alike with an overt noun but changing alif to ya with a pronoun.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r6.anchor: فقال أهل البصرة: هو مفرد لأن كلا وكلتا في توكيد الاثنين نظير «كل» في المجموع،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r7.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r7.claim: Al-Farra treats them as duals derived from كل by lightening lām and adding dual alif; they are always annexed and lack a standalone singular.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء: هو مثنى، وهو مأخوذ من كل فخففت اللام وزيدت الألف للتثنية.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r1.speaker: أهل البصرة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r1.claim: The Basrans reject the dual analysis because oblique inflection with an overt noun would require ya; the poet's shortened form is necessity, not proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r1.anchor: وهذا القول ضعيف عند أهل البصرة لأنه لو كان مثنى لوجب أن تكون ألفه في النصب والجر ياء مع الاسم الظاهر،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r2.claim: Qurtubi concludes كلا is singular in form but denotes a specific pair, unlike كل which means comprehensive totality; نحن likewise has singular form but can refer to two or more.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r2.anchor: فثبت أنه اسم مفرد كمعى، إلا أنه وضع ليدل على التثنية،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r3.claim: Jarir's line predicates a singular day of كلا, as the verse uses singular آتت; a true dual would require plural agreement.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r3.anchor: يدل على ذلك قول جرير: كلا يومي أمامة يوم صد

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r4.claim: Sibawayh says the alif of كلتا marks femininity and tā replaces an original wāw; al-Jurmi instead makes tā augment and the alif root.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r4.anchor: فقال سيبويه: ألف «كلتا» للتأنيث والتاء بدل من لام الفعل وهي واو

QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r1.claim: The gardens did not diminish any produce; God caused a river to flow through their middle.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r1.anchor: { ولم تظلم منه شيئا } أي لم تنقص. قوله تعالى: { وفجرنا خلالهما نهرا }

QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة وعاصم ويعقوب وابن أبي إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r2.claim: These readers pronounce ثمر with both consonants open, as a collective of fruit; Abu Amr uses a still mīm for kinds of wealth, while others use ḍamma on both letters.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة وعاصم ويعقوب وابن أبي إسحاق «ثمر» بفتح الثاء والميم،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says ثمر means gold, silver, and other wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ذهب وفضة وأموال.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r4.speaker: الأعمش
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r4.claim: Al-Hajjaj threatened to cut the tongue of anyone reading ثمر; al-A'mash rejected the threat and read it as a collective of fruit. Al-Nahhas finds this derivation sound but prefers the other view because the gardens bore fruit.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r4.anchor: فكان يقرأ «ثمر» ويأخذه من جمع الثمر. قال النحاس: فالتقدير على هذا القول أنه جمع ثمرة

QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r5.claim: محاورة means back-and-forth speech; nafar is a group smaller than ten and here means followers, servants, and children.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:33-34/r5.anchor: { فقال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره } أي يراجعه في الكلام ويجاوبه. والمحاورة المجاوبة،

MAJAZ:v1p401/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p401/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p401/r5.claim: ثمر is a collective noun for fruits.

RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r8.claim: Asim reads thamar with both vowels open as a plural of thimar or thamrah; Abu Amr has a still m, and the other readers round both vowels.
RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r8.anchor: قرأ عاصم بفتح الثاء والميم في الموضعين وهو جمع ثمار أو ثمرة

RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r9.claim: Abu Amr says thamar means wealth and children, supported by a poem attributed to al-Harith ibn Kalda.
RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r9.anchor: كان أبو عمرو بن العلاء يقول : الثمر المال والولد

RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r1.claim: The continuation of al-Harith ibn Kalda's cited poem says that people acquired wealth and children, supporting Abu Amr's gloss of thamar.
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r1.anchor: ولقد رأيت معاشرا … قد أثمروا مالا وولدا

RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the wealth accompanying the gardens as gold and silver cash.

RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r3.claim: Conversation is reciprocal speech, from the root meaning return, as in the verse about thinking one will not return.
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r3.anchor: والمحاورة مراجعة الكلام من قولهم : حار إذا رجع

RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r4.claim: Nafar means a man's clan and companions who defend him and go out with him.
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r4.anchor: والنفر عشيرة الرجل وأصحابه الذين يقومون بالذب عنه

RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r5.claim: The rich man vaunts his social standing and wealth over the believer.
RAZI-FULL:v21p106#2/r5.anchor: وحاصل الكلام أن الكافر ترفع على المؤمن بجاهه وماله

STUDYQURAN:18:34/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:34/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:34/r1.claim: Thamar may mean the gardens' fruit, or “profit,” meaning wealth of various kinds such as gold and silver.
STUDYQURAN:18:34/r1.anchor: thamar, here rendered “fruit,” also means“profit,” and may refer to great wealth of various kinds, including gold and silver

STUDYQURAN:18:34/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:34/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:34/r2.claim: The boast of being stronger in men means having more children, especially sons, as well as aides and servants.
STUDYQURAN:18:34/r2.anchor: meaning in children, especially sons, as well as aides and servants

STUDYQURAN:18:34/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:34/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:34/r3.claim: Wealth and children signify worldly status, but are not necessarily divine favor and cannot shield one from punishment; disbelievers make that claim at 34:35.
STUDYQURAN:18:34/r3.anchor: the Quran warns that these blessings are not necessarily signs of Divine Favor

NAHHAS:v2p456/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p456/r1.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v2p456/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash explains that the wealth and fruit belonged to one of the two men.
NAHHAS:v2p456/r1.anchor: ^ ( وكان له ثمر . . . ) ^ [ 34 ] قال الأخفش : وكان لأحدهما

TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r1.claim: Most Hijazi and Iraqi readers recite thamar with both consonants vocalized as u; some of them take it for gold and silver because these assets multiply.
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r1.anchor: وأولى القراءات في ذلك عندي بالصواب قراءة من قرأ «وكان له ثمر» بضم الثاء والميم لإجماع الحجة من القراء عليه

TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r2.claim: Mujahid interprets thamar and the later b-thamarihi as gold and silver.
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله عز وجل: {وكان له ثمر} [الكهف: 34] قال: ذهب وفضة، وفي قول الله عز وجل: {بثمره} [الكهف: 42] قال: هي أيضا ذهب وفضة

TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that thamar means a great variety of wealth.
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل عنى به: المال الكثير من صنوف الأموال

TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the word with ḍamma and glosses it as varieties of wealth or money.
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: قرأها ابن عباس: «وكان له ثمر» بالضم، وقال: يعني أنواع المال

TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r5.claim: Qatada says it means wealth of every kind.
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: «وكان له ثمر» يقول: من كل المال

TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r6.claim: Qatada also says the term covers all property, including fruit and other wealth.
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: «الثمر» المال كله، قال: وكل مال إذا اجتمع فهو ثمر

TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets thamar as the underlying principal or assets.
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: «وكان له ثمر» الثمر الأصل

TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r8.claim: Some readers keep ḍamma but suppress the mīm’s vowel for ease; this can represent either the plural of fruits or of individual fruit.
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r8.anchor: وقد قرأ بعض من وافق هؤلاء في هذه القراءة «ثمر» بضم الثاء وسكون الميم

TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r9.speaker: بعض المدنيين
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r9.claim: Some Medinan readers open both vowels, taking thamar as a plural of fruit.
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ ذلك بعض المدنيين: {وكان له ثمر} [الكهف: 34] بفتح الثاء والميم، بمعنى جمع الثمرة

TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the majority ḍamma reading by reader consensus and understands the produce as fruits from the two gardens, as the preceding description makes clear.
TAB-FULL:v15p259#2/r10.anchor: وأولى القراءات في ذلك عندي بالصواب قراءة من قرأ «وكان له ثمر» بضم الثاء والميم لإجماع الحجة من القراء عليه

TAB-FULL:v15p262/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p262/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p262/r1.claim: The garden owner boasts that he has more wealth and a stronger retinue or clan than his poorer companion.

TAB-FULL:v15p262/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p262/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p262/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī compares the boast to ʿUyayna and al-Aqraʿ asking the Prophet to remove Salman, Khabbāb, and Suhayb because they considered them inferior.
TAB-FULL:v15p262/r2.anchor: كما قال عيينة والأقرع لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: نحن سادات العرب، وأرباب الأموال، فنح عنا سلمان وخبابا وصهيبا

TAB-FULL:v15p262/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p262/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p262/r3.claim: Qatada calls wealth and a powerful following the wicked person’s worldly ambition.
TAB-FULL:v15p262/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {فقال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا} [الكهف: 34] وتلك والله أمنية الفاجر

TABATABAI:18:32-34/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r7.claim: Thamar most plausibly refers to the man's kinds of wealth, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ and al-Qāmūs; the author next allows the palm-fruit reading.
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r7.anchor: الضمير للرجل والثمر أنواع المال كما في الصحاح

TABATABAI:18:32-34/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r8.claim: An alternative takes thamar as the fruit of the palm trees.

TABATABAI:18:32-34/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r9.claim: Another alternative says the man owned wealth apart from the gardens.
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r9.anchor: وقيل المراد كان للرجل ثمر ملكه من غير جنته

TABATABAI:18:32-34/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r11.claim: Muḥāwara is reciprocal speech; nafar denotes people accompanying someone, hence its gloss as servants and children or as clan and kin.

TABATABAI:18:32-34/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r12.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r12.claim: Some gloss nafar as servants and children.

TABATABAI:18:32-34/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r13.speaker: آخرون
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r13.claim: Others gloss nafar as the man's clan and kin group.

TABATABAI:18:32-34/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r14.claim: The servants-and-children gloss fits better because the companion later contrasts his own lesser wealth and children with the boast.
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r14.anchor: والأول أوفق بما سيحكيه الله تعالى من قول صاحبه له

TABRISI:18:32-36/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:32-36/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وعاصم ويعقوب وسهل
TABRISI:18:32-36/r1.claim: These readers pronounce thamar with fatḥa in both occurrences; Ruways agrees in the first.
TABRISI:18:32-36/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وعاصم ويعقوب وسهل وكان له ثمر وأحيط بثمره في الموضعين بالفتح

TABRISI:18:32-36/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:32-36/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
TABRISI:18:32-36/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads thumr with ḍamma and a still middle consonant in both places; the remaining readers use ḍamma on both consonants.
TABRISI:18:32-36/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بضم الثاء وسكون الميم في الموضعين

TABRISI:18:32-36/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:32-36/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:18:32-36/r4.claim: Thamara is what is picked from a fruit-bearing tree; its plurals include thamarāt, thamar, and thimār by analogy with other forms.
TABRISI:18:32-36/r4.anchor: الثمرة ما يجتنى من ذي الثمر وجمعها ثمرات

TABRISI:18:32-36/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:32-36/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:18:32-36/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr's thumr may be shortened thimār, a collective plural, or a singular; any analysis allows a quiescent middle consonant.
TABRISI:18:32-36/r5.anchor: قراءة أبي عمرو وكان له ثمر يجوز أن يكون جمع ثمار كما يخفف كتب

TABRISI:18:32-36/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:32-36/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:18:32-36/r6.claim: Some linguists distinguish thamar as wealth from thumr as edible fruit; exegetes similarly take the word for palms and trees, not their fruit.
TABRISI:18:32-36/r6.anchor: وقال بعض أهل اللغة الثمر المال والثمر المأكول

TABRISI:18:32-36/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:32-36/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:32-36/r7.claim: The reference may be fruit-bearing trees rather than fruit: expenditure was on productive roots, and the affliction uprooted them.
TABRISI:18:32-36/r7.anchor: بل الأصول التي تحمل الثمرة لا نفس الثمر

TABRISI:18:32-36/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:32-36/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:32-36/r8.claim: The garden's greenery was erased by the calamity, becoming like a black night or white day.
TABRISI:18:32-36/r8.anchor: وما بطل من خضرتها بالآفة النازلة بها

TABRISI:18:32-36/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:32-36/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو
TABRISI:18:32-36/r9.claim: Thumr can mean kinds of wealth; destruction of that wealth includes crops. This makes the readings with thumr clearer than fatḥa, though fatḥa may report only part of the loss.
TABRISI:18:32-36/r9.anchor: وحكي عن أبي عمرو ثمر والثمر أنواع المال

TABRISI:18:32-33/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:32-33/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:32-33/r2.claim: Muḥāwarah means reciprocal speech; it is also said someone gave no response or reply.

TABRISI:18:33-36/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:33-36/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:33-36/r1.claim: One explanation is that the palm trees bore fruit; another is that the man owned fruit independently of the gardens.

TABRISI:18:33-36/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:33-36/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:18:33-36/r2.claim: The man's other wealth alongside the gardens was gold and silver.
TABRISI:18:33-36/r2.anchor: كان لهذا الرجل مع هذين البستانين الذهب والفضة عن مجاهد

TABRISI:18:33-36/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:33-36/r3.speaker: قتادة وابن عباس
TABRISI:18:33-36/r3.claim: The man's other wealth consisted of all kinds of property.
TABRISI:18:33-36/r3.anchor: كان له معهما جميع الأموال عن قتادة وابن عباس

TABRISI:18:33-36/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:33-36/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:33-36/r4.claim: The unbelieving garden owner says he has more wealth and greater standing; nafar names a clan because they accompany him on errands.
TABRISI:18:33-36/r4.anchor: أي أعز عشيرة ورهطا وسمى العشيرة نفرا

TABRISI:18:33-36/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:33-36/r5.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
TABRISI:18:33-36/r5.claim: Aʿaz nafaran may instead mean more servants and children.
TABRISI:18:33-36/r5.anchor: معناه أعز خدما وولدا عن قتادة ومقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, in the report through Ali ibn Abi Talha, says thamar means wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية علي بن أبي طلحة في قوله: {ثمر}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r5.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r5.claim: Mujahid says the man's thamar was gold and silver.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r6.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r6.claim: Qatada says he possessed every kind of wealth.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r7.claim: Readers differ: most read thamar with both vowels rounded, Abu Amr rounds the first and quiets the second, and Asim opens both.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r7.anchor: واختلف القراء في قوله: {ثمر} علي ثلاثة أوجه: ثمر بضم الثاء والميم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r8.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r8.claim: Al-Layth says thamar is the fruit borne by a tree.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r9.claim: Thamar can mean types of wealth; athmara can mean that a man's wealth increased, and thammara that God increased someone's wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r9.anchor: والثمر أنواع المال، يقال: أثمر الرجل إذا كثر ماله، وثمر الله مال فلان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r10.speaker: الفراء عن مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r10.claim: Al-Farra transmits Mujahid's distinction: Qur'anic thamar means wealth, while thamar means fruits.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r10.anchor: وروى الفراء بإسناده عن مجاهد قال: (ما كان في القرآن من ثمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd distinguishes thamar as the orchard's stock or trees from thamara as what is gathered from a fruit tree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r11.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: (الثمر الأصل، والثمرة ما يجتنى من ذي الثمر)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r12.claim: The noun thamara has several plurals, including thamrat, thimar, and thamar, by analogy with common broken-plural patterns.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r13.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r13.claim: Abu Amr's shortened reading can be a lightened plural of thimar, a plural of thamara, or a singular thamar; any of these analyses permits a silent middle consonant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p9/r13.anchor: فقراءة أبي عمرو بالتخفيف تحتمل ثلاثة أوجه أحدها: أن يكون جمع ثمار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:33-37/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:33-37/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:33-37/r2.claim: The unbelieving brother had abundant property; when asked what he had spent it on, he said he had invested it for the Hereafter.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:33-37/r2.anchor: وذلك أنه سأله عن ماله فيما أنفقه؟ فقال: قدمته بين يدي لأقدم عليه،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:33-37/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:33-37/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:33-37/r3.claim: The brother boasted that he had more wealth and a stronger clan or tribe.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:33-37/r3.anchor: { أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا } رهطا وعشيرة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r4.claim: The word thamar is read in two ways: thamar denotes the original wealth, while thumur denotes fruit.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r4.anchor: وهي تقرأ على وجهين: ثمر وهو الأصل.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r5.claim: Qatada takes thamar in the first reading to mean wealth.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r6.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r6.claim: Mujahid specifies the wealth as gold and silver.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r9.claim: The two men were conversing by exchanging words, and more numerous means more men and supporters.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p185/r9.anchor: المحاورة: مراجعة الكلام. } أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا { [الكهف: 34] أكثر رجالا وناصرا.

SAMIN-DURR:18:34/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:34/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:18:34/r1.claim: Thamar with ḍamma means wealth; Ibn ʿAbbās says it includes gold, silver, livestock, and all other property, while another view restricts it to gold and silver. The Nābigha’s line witnesses athmara for wealth and children; Abū Rajāʾ reads bi-thamarihi with fatḥa and a quiescent mīm.
SAMIN-DURR:18:34/r1.anchor: وتقدم أن " الثمر " بالضم المال. فقال ابن عباس: جميع المال من ذهب

SAMIN-DURR:18:34/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:34/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:34/r2.claim: Wa-huwa yuḥāwiruhu is a circumstantial clause clarifying dialogue, since mere speech does not entail conversation; muḥāwara is reciprocal speech from ḥāra, ‘returned,’ as in 84:14 and Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse about a meteor turning to ash. It may describe subject or object.
SAMIN-DURR:18:34/r2.anchor: " وهو يحاوره " جملة حالية مبينة إذ لا يلزم من القول المحاورة؛

ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r1.claim: Thamar can mean tree produce, wealth, or a plural of thamrah, but fruit is preferable here because the gardens’ yield was already mentioned; thimār and thamar are also forms.
ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r1.anchor:
والثمر ههنا أحسن، لأن قوله: (كلتا الجنتين آتت أكلها).
قد دل على الثمر،

ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r2.claim: Mālan and nafarā are accusative specifications; the boast says he has more wealth and more numerous supporters.
ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r2.anchor: مالا، ونفرا، منصوبان على التمييز، وأخبره أنه أعز منه ناصرا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads thamar and bi-thamarihi with ḍamma on thāʾ and a quiescent mīm; two transmitters report his reading like Nāfiʿ's instead.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: (ثمر) [الكهف/ 34] و (بثمره) [42] بضم الثاء وسكون الميم

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r2.claim: They use ḍamma on both thāʾ and mīm in both occurrences.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: (ثمر) و (بثمره) مضمومة الثاء والميم

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r3.speaker: علي بن نصر وحسين الجعفي عن أبي عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r3.claim: These transmitters report Abū ʿAmr reading thamar like Nāfiʿ, with both vowels rounded.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r3.anchor: علي بن نصر، وحسين الجعفي، عن أبي عمرو: (ثمر) مثل نافع

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r4.speaker: عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r4.claim: ʿĀṣim reads both words with fatḥa on thāʾ and mīm.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r4.anchor: وقرأ عاصم: ثمر وبثمره، بفتح الثاء والميم فيهما

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r5.claim: Thamara is fruit harvested from a fruit-bearing plant; its plural can be thamarāt or thimār, and thimār can itself be reduced to thamar like kitāb/kutub.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r5.anchor: الثمرة: ما يجتنى من ذي الثمرة، وجمعه: ثمرات

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r6.claim: The light-reading thamar may be a plural of thimār or thamara, or a singular noun; any analysis permits a quiescent middle consonant and also applies to verse 42.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r6.anchor: فعلى أي هذه الوجوه كان جاز إسكان العين منه وساغ

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r7.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r7.claim: Some linguists distinguish thamar as wealth from thumr as edible produce; reports also gloss it as the trees that bear fruit, rather than the fruit itself.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r7.anchor: وقال بعض أهل اللغة: الثمر: المال، والثمر: المأكول

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r8.claim: The interpretation as the garden's fruit-bearing trees fits the mention of what the owner spent on it; the disaster destroyed the roots, like the other garden described as burned or barren.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p142/r8.anchor: الأصول التي تحمل الثمرة، لا نفس الثمر

QIRAAT-ER:18:34:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:34:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:34:4#1/r1.claim: The vowel shift gives thumurun a plural sense, “fruits” or “varieties of wealth,” broadening the man's possessions.

QIRAAT-ER:18:34:4#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:34:4#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:34:4#2/r1.claim: Sukūn on mīm compresses thumur, retaining the same semantic range as a phonological variant.
QIRAAT-ER:18:34:4#2/r1.anchor: Sukūn on mīm; compressed form of thumur — same semantic range

QIRAAT-ER:18:34:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:34:12#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:34:12#1/r1.claim: The short ana without madd gives a clipped delivery.
QIRAAT-ER:18:34:12#1/r1.anchor: Short form without madd — reduced pronoun, clipped delivery

QIRAAT-ER:18:34:12#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:34:12#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:34:12#2/r1.claim: Madd on the final alif prolongs self-reference and iconically mirrors self-aggrandizement.
QIRAAT-ER:18:34:12#2/r1.anchor: Extended madd on final alif — prolonged self-reference; the elongation iconically mirrors self-aggrandizement

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#3/r1.claim: Mujāhid says the garden owner's thar was gold and silver.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#3/r1.anchor: عن رجل عن مجاهد ﴿ وكان له ثمر ﴾ قال الذهب والفضة

BAQILLANI:v1p142/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p142/r1.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
BAQILLANI:v1p142/r1.claim: ʿUthmān says the religion’s affliction is its faultfinders and suspicious people, who flatter publicly, conceal hostility, and follow whoever first calls them.
BAQILLANI:v1p142/r1.anchor: إن لكل شيء آفة وإن لكل نعمة عاهة وإن عاهة هذا الدين عيابون ظنانون يظهرون لكم ما تحبون ويسرون ما تكرهون

BAQILLANI:v1p142/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p142/r2.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
BAQILLANI:v1p142/r2.claim: He argues that they accepted ʿUmar’s authority despite greater complaints, because ʿUmar restrained and reprimanded them.
