BAQILLANI:v1p142/r2.anchor: لقد أقررتم لابن الخطاب بأكثر مما نقمتم علي ولكنه وقمكم وقمعكم وزجركم زجر النعام المخزمة

BAQILLANI:v1p142/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p142/r3.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
BAQILLANI:v1p142/r3.claim: ʿUthmān defends his strength and claim to leadership, asking whether the community lacks any right and why he should not act as he wishes if he is imam.
BAQILLANI:v1p142/r3.anchor: هل تفقدون من حقوقكم شيئا فما لي لا أفعل في الحق ما أشاء إذا فلم كنت إماما

BAQILLANI:v1p14/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r1.claim: The Qurʾān itself is the proof of the Prophet’s mission: God made the Prophet’s heart the repository of revelation and could have withheld it from him.
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r1.anchor: فدل على أنه جعل قلبه مستودعا لوحيه ومستنزلا لكتابه وأنه لو شاء صرف ذلك عنه إلى غيره

BAQILLANI:v1p14/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r2.claim: The Prophet’s prophethood rests on the Qurʾān’s proof and miracle; the Qurʾān demonstrates its own divine origin and truth.
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r2.anchor: فبان بهذا وبنظائره ما قلنا من أن بناء نبوته على دلالة القرآن ومعجزته وصار له من الحكم في دلالته على نفسه وصدقه

BAQILLANI:v1p14/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r3.claim: Other revealed books require an additional sign because their composition is not miraculous, even though reports of unseen matters within them may be miraculous.
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r3.anchor: وفارق حكمه حكم غيره من الكتب المنزلة على الأنبياء لأنها لا تدل على أنفسها إلا بأمر زائد عليها

BAQILLANI:v1p14/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r4.claim: The Qurʾān shares the other scriptures’ evidentiary content and adds inimitable composition, so it can itself identify its source.
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r4.anchor: وليس كذلك القرآن لأنه يشاركها في هذه الدلالة ويزيد عليها في أن نظمه معجز فيمكن أن يستدل به عليه

BAQILLANI:v1p14/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r5.claim: Moses knew God’s speech directly by hearing God speak; people who hear or recite the Qurʾān know by inference that it is God’s speech, a shared conclusion through different means.
BAQILLANI:v1p14/r5.anchor: لأن موسى عليه السلام لما سمع كلامه علم أنه في الحقيقة كلامه وكذلك من يسمع القرآن يعلم أنه كلام الله

BURHAN:v4p172/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p172/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p172/r1.claim: The comparison standard can be omitted and inferred in وأعز نفرا; omission is common when an afعل comparative is the predicate.
BURHAN:v4p172/r1.anchor: ويكثر ذلك إذا كان افعل التفضيل خبرا

BURHAN:v4p172/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p172/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p172/r2.claim: When attached in a comparative construction, afعل takes a definite plural; Zayd is not usefully called better than an indefinite man or men, but may be best of the men.
BURHAN:v4p172/r2.anchor: وحيث اضيف إنما يضاف إلى جمع معرف نحو أحكم الحاكمين ولا يجوز زيد أفضل رجل ولا افضل رجال لأنه لا فائدة فيه

BURHAN:v4p172/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p172/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p172/r4.claim: An indefinite collective noun may follow afعل because أفضل القوم is a singular form, not a plural form, and is therefore treated more lightly.
BURHAN:v4p172/r4.anchor: قلت لأن أفضل القوم ليس من ألفاظ الجموع بل من الألفاظ المفردة فخففوه بترك الألف واللام الثانية

BURHAN:v4p172/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p172/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p172/r5.claim: With the definite article or in a construct, afعل can be dual or plural, as in الأرذلون, الأخسرين, أكابر, and أراذلنا.
BURHAN:v4p172/r5.anchor: إذا كان أفعل بالألف واللام أو مضافا جاز تثنيته وجمعه

BURHAN:v4p170/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p170/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p170/r6.claim: Afعل has three patterns: construct, definite with al, or unmarked and linked to من introducing the compared item.
BURHAN:v4p170/r6.anchor: السابعة أفعل في الكلام على ثلاثة أضرب مضاف

ITQAN:v4p367/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p367/r1.claim: A sound report describes Moses as tall, dark-complexioned, curly-haired, and resembling a man from Shanuʾa.
ITQAN:v4p367/r1.anchor: وفي الصحيح وصفه أنه ( آدم طوال جعد كأنه من رجال شنوءة )

ITQAN:v4p367/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r2.speaker: الثعلبي
ITQAN:v4p367/r2.anchor: قال الثعلبي عاش مائة وعشرين سنة

ITQAN:v4p367/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r3.speaker: الكرماني
ITQAN:v4p367/r3.claim: The source reports three views about Aaron’s kinship to Moses: full brother, brother only through his mother, or brother only through his father; al-Kirmani cites the latter two.
ITQAN:v4p367/r3.anchor: هارون أخوه شقيقه وقيل لأمه فقط وقيل لأبيه فقط حكاهما الكرماني في عجائبه

ITQAN:v4p367/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p367/r4.claim: Aaron was taller and very eloquent, died before Moses, and had been born one year earlier.
ITQAN:v4p367/r4.anchor: كان أطول منه فصيحا جدا مات قبل موسى وكان ولد قبله بسنة

ITQAN:v4p367/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p367/r5.claim: In an account of the Night Journey, the Prophet meets Aaron in the fifth heaven, sees one half of his long beard white and the other black, and Gabriel identifies him as beloved among his people.
ITQAN:v4p367/r5.anchor: وفي بعض أحاديث الإسراء صعدت إلى السماء الخامسة فإذا أنا بهارون ونصف لحيته بيضاء ونصفها أسود

ITQAN:v4p367/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r6.speaker: ابن مسكويه
ITQAN:v4p367/r6.claim: Ibn Miskawayh says the Hebrew meaning of Hārūn is the beloved one.
ITQAN:v4p367/r6.anchor: وذكر ابن مسكويه أن معنى هارون بالعبرانية ( المحبب )

ITQAN:v4p367/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p367/r7.claim: The source gives David’s ancestry from his father Jesse through Obed, Boaz, Salmon, Nahshon, Amminadab, Ram, Hezron, Perez, Judah, and Jacob.
ITQAN:v4p367/r7.anchor: داود هو ابن إيشى بكسر الهمزة وسكون التحتية وبالشين المعجمة بن عوبد بوزن جعفر

ITQAN:v4p367/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r8.speaker: كعب
ITQAN:v4p367/r8.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports David as the most devout of humanity; Kaʿb describes him as handsome, red-faced, white-bodied, long-bearded, beautiful-voiced, and granted both prophethood and kingship.
ITQAN:v4p367/r8.anchor: في الترمذي أنه كان أعبد البشر قال كعب كان أحمر الوجه سبط الرأس أبيض الجسم طويل اللحية

ITQAN:v4p367/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r9.speaker: النووي
ITQAN:v4p367/r9.claim: Al-Nawawi says historians report that David lived 100 years, reigned for 40, and had twelve sons.
ITQAN:v4p367/r9.anchor: قال النووي قال أهل التاريخ عاش مائة سنة مدة ملكه منها أربعون سنة وكان له اثنا عشر ابنا

ITQAN:v4p367/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r10.speaker: كعب
ITQAN:v4p367/r10.claim: Kaʿb describes Solomon as handsome, physically substantial, devout, humble, and consulted by his father from a young age because of his intelligence and knowledge.
ITQAN:v4p367/r10.anchor: قال كعب كان أبيض جسيما وسيما وضيئا جميلا خاشعا متواضعا وكان أبوه يشاوره في كثير من أموره

ITQAN:v4p367/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p367/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report from Ibn Jubayr, names Solomon and Dhul-Qarnayn as believing kings of the earth, and Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar as unbelieving kings.
ITQAN:v4p367/r11.anchor: وأخرج ابن جبير عن ابن عباس قال ملك الأرض مؤمنان سليمان وذو القرنين وكافران نمروذ وبخت نصر

ITQAN:v4p367/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r12.speaker: أهل التاريخ
ITQAN:v4p367/r12.claim: Historians say Solomon became king at thirteen, began building the Temple four years into his reign, and died aged fifty-three.
ITQAN:v4p367/r12.anchor: قال أهل التاريخ ملك وهو ابن ثلاث عشرة سنة وابتدأ بناء بيت المقدس بعد ملكه بأربع سنين ومات وله ثلاث وخمسون سنة

ITQAN:v4p367/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r13.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ITQAN:v4p367/r13.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Job was an Israelite and that no reliable genealogy is established for him beyond his father’s name, Abyad.
ITQAN:v4p367/r13.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق الصحيح أنه كان من بني إسرائيل ولم يصح في نسبه شيء إلا أن اسم أبيه أبيض

ITQAN:v4p367/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r14.speaker: ابن جرير
ITQAN:v4p367/r14.claim: Ibn Jarir gives Job’s lineage as Ayyub son of Mus, son of Ruh, son of Esau, son of Isaac.
ITQAN:v4p367/r14.anchor: وقال ابن جرير هو أيوب بن موص بن روح بن عيص بن إسحاق

ITQAN:v4p367/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p367/r15.speaker: ابن عساكر
ITQAN:v4p367/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAsakir reports that Job’s mother was Lot’s daughter and his father believed in Abraham, which would place Job before Moses.
ITQAN:v4p367/r15.anchor: وحكى ابن عساكر أن أمه بنت لوط وأن أباه ممن آمن بإبراهيم وعلى هذا فكان قبل موسى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p105/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p105/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p105/r3.claim: Fronting an object makes the denial challenge whether that person is fit to receive the action at all; أزيدا تضرب questions whether anyone could dare strike Zayd.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p105/r3.anchor: تقديم إسم المفعول يقتضي أن يكون الإنكار في طريق الإحالة والمنع

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p188/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p188/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p188/r1.claim: Sentences like adjective and noun, or emphasis and what it emphasizes, are so closely joined that conjunction would be like coordinating a thing with itself.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p188/r1.anchor: فلا يكون فيها العطف البتة لشبه العطف فيها لو عطفت بعطف الشيء على نفسه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p188/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p188/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p188/r2.claim: Conjoin a sentence that is distinct from its predecessor but shares its syntactic role, such as two subjects or two objects.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p188/r2.anchor: ويدخل معه في معنى مثل أن يكون كلا الاسمين فاعلا أو مفعولا أو مضافا إليه فيكون حقها العطف

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p188/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p188/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p188/r3.claim: A wholly unrelated sentence takes no conjunction; thus omission of conjunction signals either maximal connection or complete separation, while conjunction marks an intermediate relation.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p188/r3.anchor: فترك العطف يكون إما للاتصال إلى الغاية أو الانفصال إلى الغاية

DAMGHANI:v1p274/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r4.claim: Al-ṣāḥib can mean a brother, as in the exchange between the two men in the garden narrative.
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r4.anchor: قال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره يعني لاخيه مثلها فيها قال له صاحبه يعني اخاه

DAMGHANI:v1p93/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p93/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p93/r8.claim: With ḍamma on mīm, thamar means wealth in the account of the two garden owners.
DAMGHANI:v1p93/r8.anchor: فوجه منها الثمر مضموما هو المال قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف وكان له ثمر يعني المال

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r1.claim: The fragment glosses تصفر as being empty of affection.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r2.claim: المكفوفة means المشرجة: folded over; Shammākh’s verse uses مشرج for what is concealed within the chest.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r2.anchor: قال الشماخ : وكادت غداة البين ينطق طرفها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r3.claim: In the Prophet’s phrase about finding his Lord’s نفس from Yemen, نفس means relief, which came to him through the Anṣār.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r3.anchor: أجد نفس ربكم من قبل اليمن

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r5.speaker: عمر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r5.claim: ʿUmar likewise said that the wind is from God’s روح and should not be cursed.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r5.anchor: تقول عمر رضي الله عنه: الريح من روح الله فلا تسبوها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r6.claim: Abū Bakr’s ‘handful of God’s handfuls’ means that even if numerous, they are few before God, like what a person holds in one hand; حفنة is a handful given or taken.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r6.anchor: وقول أبي بكر رضي الله عنه: نحن حفنة من حفنات الله

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r7.speaker: بعضهم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r7.claim: Some explain ʿUmar’s proverb as ‘perhaps the little cave hides misfortunes’; it is attributed to Bihays, who killed his brothers’ murderers in a cave and was then pursued for vengeance.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r7.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هو تصغير غار. وهو مثل للعرب. ويقال: إن أول من قاله بيهس

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r8.claim: Another explanation takes al-Ghuwayr to be a water source rather than a small cave.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r9.claim: ʿAlī’s saying that one whose father has many sons can gird himself with them means many brothers provide protection; the belt symbolizes support for the back.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r9.anchor: وقول علي كرم الله وجه: من يطل هن أبيه ينتطق به

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r10.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r10.claim: An unnamed poet illustrates the proverb with al-Ḥārith ibn Sadūs, who had twenty-one sons, as an example of strength through many brothers.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r10.anchor: قول الشاعر : فلو شاء ربي كان أير أبيكم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r11.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r11.speaker: عمر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r11.claim: ʿUmar’s rule is that an emir’s pledge made without consultation establishes neither the pledger nor the pledged as ruler, since both could be killed; authority requires a public gathering’s agreement.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p304/r11.anchor: وقول عمر رضي الله عنه: أيما رجل بايع عن غير مشاورة، فلا يؤمر واحد منهما

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p41/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p41/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p41/r1.claim: Umar, enraged after learning that his sister Fatima and her husband Sa'id ibn Zayd had converted, heard quiet recitation from Ta-Ha, read the sheet, and pledged allegiance to the Prophet.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p41/r1.anchor: فما كاد يدنو من الباب حتى سمع تلاوة خافتة لآيات من سرة طه، فدخل يلح فى طلب الصحيفة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p41/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p41/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p41/r2.claim: After the pledge of al-Aqaba, the Prophet sent Mus'ab ibn Umayr to Yathrib to teach the Qur'an and Islam; he stayed with As'ad ibn Zurara.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p41/r2.anchor: ندب صاحبه مصعب بن عمير ليذهب مع أصحاب العقبة إلى يثرب، ليقرئهم القرآن ويعلمهم الإسلام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p41/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p41/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p41/r3.claim: When Mus'ab and As'ad visited Banu Abd al-Ashhal, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh sent Usayd ibn Hudayr to drive them away; Usayd arrived with a spear and challenged them.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p41/r3.anchor: لا أبا لك! انطلق إلى هذين الرجلين فازجرهما وانههما عن أن يأتيا ديارنا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir read to Mujahid, whose reading came through Ibn Abbas from Ubayy; Ibn Mujahid says Ibn Kathir never differed from Mujahid's recitation.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r1.anchor: قرأ على مجاهد بن جبر وقرأ مجاهد على ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وقرأ ابن عباس على أبي

IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r2.claim: Ibn Muhaysin, a contemporary Meccan reader, studied with Darbas, Ibn Abbas's freedman; Ibn Kathir also read to Darbas.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r2.anchor: وقد قرأ ابن كثير أيضا على درباس

IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r3.claim: Ibn Muhaysin was learned in Arabic, had an independent reading choice, and had also studied with Mujahid.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r3.anchor: وكان ابن محيصن عالما بالعربية وكان له اختيار لم يتبع فيه أصحابه وأخذ عن مجاهد أيضا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r4.claim: Mujahid reportedly praised Ibn Muhaysin as someone who builds and firmly arranges matters in Arabic.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r4.anchor: ويروى عن مجاهد أنه كان يقول ابن محيصن يبني ويرصص في العربية

IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r5.claim: Meccans did not unite around Ibn Muhaysin's reading as they did around Ibn Kathir's.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r5.anchor: ولم يجمع أهل مكة على قراءته كما أجمعوا على قراءة ابن كثير

IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r6.speaker: حميد بن قيس
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r6.claim: Hamid ibn Qays al-Sandali also read with Mujahid in Mecca and did not differ from his recitation.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r6.anchor: وكان حميد بن قيس أخو عمر بن قيس سندل أيضا بمكة قرأ على مجاهد

IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r7.claim: Ibn Mujahid says the Meccans remain united on Ibn Kathir's reading.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p64#2/r7.anchor: أجمع أهل مكة على قراءته إلى اليوم ابن كثير
